question: In a circle with center O, PQ and RS are two chords. PQ and RS, when produced, meet at point K. If PR is a diameter and ∠PKS = 66°, what is the value of ∠QOS?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 48°.

GIVEN

• Two chords PQ and RS produced meet outside the circle at K; PR is a diameter; ∠PKS = 66°.

SOLUTION

• Angle between two secants from an external point = ½ (difference of intercepted arcs).

• So ∠K = ½ (arc PR − arc QS).

• PR is a diameter ⇒ arc PR = 180°.

• 66 = ½ (180 − arc QS) ⇒ 132 = 180 − arc QS ⇒ arc QS = 48°.

• ∠QOS is the central angle standing on arc QS, so ∠QOS = arc QS = 48°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• External angle = ½(far arc − near arc). With the diameter giving the far arc = 180°, near arc = 180 − 2×66 = 48° directly, and the central angle equals that arc.

NOTE

• Two-secant angle = ½|difference of intercepted arcs|; a central angle equals the arc it subtends, while an inscribed angle is half of it.

question: 86 − 42 + 97 − (27 + 22) + 49 × 2 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 190.

GIVEN

• 86 − 42 + 97 − (27 + 22) + 49 × 2

SOLUTION

• Brackets: (27 + 22) = 49.

• Multiplication: 49 × 2 = 98.

• Now: 86 − 42 + 97 − 49 + 98 = 44 + 97 − 49 + 98.

• = 141 − 49 + 98 = 92 + 98 = 190.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Group positives and negatives: positives 86 + 97 + 98 = 281; negatives 42 + 49 = 91; 281 − 91 = 190.

NOTE

• Follow BODMAS: Brackets → Of → Division/Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction, working left to right.

question: 87 + (29 × 1) − 36 + 33 ÷ 3 + 14 − 18 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 87.

GIVEN

• 87 + (29 × 1) − 36 + 33 ÷ 3 + 14 − 18

SOLUTION

• (29 × 1) = 29 and 33 ÷ 3 = 11.

• Now: 87 + 29 − 36 + 11 + 14 − 18.

• = 116 − 36 + 11 + 14 − 18 = 80 + 11 + 14 − 18.

• = 91 + 14 − 18 = 105 − 18 = 87.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Positives: 87 + 29 + 11 + 14 = 141; negatives: 36 + 18 = 54; 141 − 54 = 87.

NOTE

• Resolve division and multiplication before doing additions and subtractions (BODMAS).

question:
The line chart given below shows the number of calories burnt by a person on 6 consecutive days DY1, DY2, DY3, DY4, DY5 and DY6.

What is the average number of calories burnt by the person each day in the given 6 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 595.5.

GIVEN

• Calories: DY1 = 698, DY2 = 596, DY3 = 266, DY4 = 621, DY5 = 690, DY6 = 702.

SOLUTION

• Total = 698 + 596 + 266 + 621 + 690 + 702 = 3573.

• Average = 3573 ÷ 6 = 595.5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair values to add fast: (698 + 702) + (596 + 690) + (266 + 621) = 1400 + 1286 + 887 = 3573, then ÷ 6 = 595.5.

NOTE

• Average = (sum of all observations) ÷ (number of observations).

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of milk shops in 6 towns. The data is presented in the terms of percent.

Central angle formed by sector of which town is 21.6 degrees more than the central angle formed by the sector of town A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. F.

GIVEN

• Town percentages: A = 12%, B = 10%, C = 15%, D = 14%, E = 31%, F = 18%.

SOLUTION

• Central angle of A = 12% × 360° = 43.2°.

• Required angle = 43.2° + 21.6° = 64.8°.

• Percentage for 64.8° = 64.8 ÷ 360 × 100 = 18%, which is town F.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 21.6° in a pie = 21.6 ÷ 3.6 = 6 percentage points. So required town = A's 12% + 6% = 18% = town F.

NOTE

• In a pie chart, 1% corresponds to 3.6° (since 100% = 360°); central angle = percentage × 3.6.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of banks in 5 cities. The data is presented in the terms of percent. Difference between the total number of banks in N and Q and total number of banks in L and M = 2500.

What is the ratio of number of banks in N to the total number of banks in P and Q?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3 : 4.

GIVEN

• City percentages: L = 10%, M = 20%, N = 30%, P = 15%, Q = 25%.

SOLUTION

• Banks in N = 30%.

• Total banks in P and Q = 15% + 25% = 40%.

• Ratio N : (P + Q) = 30 : 40 = 3 : 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Since every share is out of the same total, just use the percentages directly: 30 : 40 = 3 : 4 (the 2500 clue is not needed here).

NOTE

• For ratios drawn from one pie chart, the percentages themselves form the ratio — the common total cancels.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of mobile phones sold by the given 5 brands in a month.

A = Total number of mobile phones sold by brand X and Y.

B = Total number of mobile phones sold by brand Z and U.

What is the value of A : B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 61 : 76.

GIVEN

• Sales: X = 320, Y = 290, Z = 410, U = 350, V = 270.

SOLUTION

• A = X + Y = 320 + 290 = 610.

• B = Z + U = 410 + 350 = 760.

• A : B = 610 : 760 = 61 : 76 (dividing both by 10).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Drop the common zero at once: 610 : 760 → 61 : 76 (no further common factor).

NOTE

• Simplify ratios by cancelling common factors; here HCF of 610 and 760 is 10.

question: In a triangle, sides are proportional to 7:9:14. If the shortest side is 14 cm, find the perimeter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 60 cm.

GIVEN

• Sides in ratio 7 : 9 : 14; shortest side = 14 cm.

SOLUTION

• Shortest ratio term is 7, which equals 14 cm ⇒ 1 part = 14 ÷ 7 = 2 cm.

• Sides = 14, 18, 28 cm.

• Perimeter = (7 + 9 + 14) × 2 = 30 × 2 = 60 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Perimeter = (sum of ratio parts ÷ smallest part) × shortest side = (30 ÷ 7) × 14 = 60 cm.

NOTE

• When sides are given as a ratio, one 'part' = actual length ÷ its ratio term; multiply the total ratio by that part.

question: Arrange the following values in ascending order.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2½ < 22/6 < 3⅚ < 26/6.

GIVEN

• Values: 3⅚, 26/6, 2½, 22/6.

SOLUTION

• Convert to decimals: 3⅚ = 23/6 = 3.833…, 26/6 = 4.333…, 2½ = 2.5, 22/6 = 3.667….

• Ascending order: 2.5 < 3.667 < 3.833 < 4.333.

• That is 2½ < 22/6 < 3⅚ < 26/6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Write all over denominator 6: 2½ = 15/6, 22/6, 3⅚ = 23/6, 26/6 → compare only numerators 15 < 22 < 23 < 26.

NOTE

• To compare fractions quickly, express them with a common denominator and simply order the numerators.

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 0.43.

GIVEN

• (0.12 ÷ 0.3) + (0.015 ÷ 0.5)

SOLUTION

• 0.12 ÷ 0.3 = 12 ÷ 30 = 0.4.

• 0.015 ÷ 0.5 = 15 ÷ 500 = 0.03.

• Sum = 0.4 + 0.03 = 0.43.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Cancel the decimals by scaling: 0.12/0.3 → 1.2/3 = 0.4; 0.015/0.5 → 0.15/5 = 0.03; add to get 0.43.

NOTE

• Dividing decimals: multiply numerator and denominator by the same power of 10 to make the divisor a whole number.

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 6/25.

GIVEN

• 1/(9 + √6) + 1/(9 − √6)

SOLUTION

• Combine over a common denominator: [(9 − √6) + (9 + √6)] ÷ [(9 + √6)(9 − √6)].

• Numerator = 18; Denominator = 9² − (√6)² = 81 − 6 = 75.

• = 18/75 = 6/25.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For 1/(a+√b) + 1/(a−√b), answer = 2a/(a²−b) = 18/75 = 6/25 in one step.

NOTE

• (a + √b)(a − √b) = a² − b; adding conjugate reciprocals cancels the surd, leaving 2a over a² − b.

question: The sum of the three consecutive even numbers is 30. What is the sum of the smallest and the largest of the three numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 20.

GIVEN

• Three consecutive even numbers with sum = 30.

SOLUTION

• Let them be x − 2, x, x + 2 ⇒ 3x = 30 ⇒ x = 10.

• Numbers are 8, 10, 12.

• Sum of smallest and largest = 8 + 12 = 20.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For an odd count of numbers in AP, the middle term = sum ÷ 3 = 10; smallest + largest = 2 × middle = 20.

NOTE

• In any AP, terms equidistant from the middle add up to twice the middle term.

question: What is the remainder when 741 is divided by 9?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Divide 741 by 9 and find the remainder.

SOLUTION

• 9 × 82 = 738, and 741 − 738 = 3.

• So remainder = 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Remainder on division by 9 = digit sum mod 9: 7 + 4 + 1 = 12 → 1 + 2 = 3.

NOTE

• A number leaves the same remainder on division by 9 (and by 3) as the sum of its digits.

question: 28P0 is divisible by 8. Which of the following cannot be the value of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1.

GIVEN

• Number 28P0 is divisible by 8; find the value P cannot take.

SOLUTION

• Divisibility by 8 depends on the last three digits '8P0' = 800 + 10P.

• 800 is divisible by 8, so 10P must be divisible by 8, i.e. P must be a multiple of 4.

• Allowed: P = 0 (2800), 4 (2840), 8 (2880); P = 1 gives 2810, which is not divisible by 8.

• So P cannot be 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the last 3 digits decide divisibility by 8; test each option: 2810 ÷ 8 = 351.25 → not divisible, so 1 is the odd one out.

NOTE

• A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

question: Average of 6 numbers is P. One number is removed. New average is P + 5. Which number was removed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. P − 25.

GIVEN

• 6 numbers have average P; after removing one, 5 numbers have average P + 5.

SOLUTION

• Total of 6 numbers = 6P.

• Total of remaining 5 numbers = 5(P + 5) = 5P + 25.

• Removed number = 6P − (5P + 25) = P − 25.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Removing a number raised the average of the rest by 5 across 5 numbers, i.e. the removed value is 5×5 = 25 below the old average P → P − 25.

NOTE

• Removed value = old total − new total; when the average rises after removal, the removed term is below the original average.

question: Average age of a group of 16 boys is 24 years. Two boys with ages 19 years and 18 years left the group. One boy with age 43 years joined the group. What is the new average age (in years) of the group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 26.

GIVEN

• 16 boys, average 24 yrs; two boys (19, 18) leave; one boy (43) joins.

SOLUTION

• Total age of 16 boys = 16 × 24 = 384.

• After two leave: 384 − 19 − 18 = 347 (now 14 boys).

• After one joins: 347 + 43 = 390 (now 15 boys).

• New average = 390 ÷ 15 = 26 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Net change in total = 43 − (19 + 18) = +6; new count = 15. New total 390 ÷ 15 = 26.

NOTE

• Track the total and the count separately: new average = adjusted total ÷ new number of members.

question:
In the given figure, angle ABD = 110 degrees and angle ACE = 125 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BAC?

[Figure: Points D, B, C, E lie on a straight line in that order; A is above the line, forming triangle ABC with ∠ABD and ∠ACE as exterior angles at B and C.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 55.

GIVEN

• D, B, C, E are collinear; ∠ABD = 110°, ∠ACE = 125°.

SOLUTION

• ∠ABD is the exterior angle at B ⇒ ∠BAC + ∠ACB = 110°.

• ∠ACE is the exterior angle at C ⇒ ∠BAC + ∠ABC = 125°.

• Adding: 2∠BAC + (∠ABC + ∠ACB) = 235°, and ∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°.

• So 2∠BAC + (180° − ∠BAC) = 235° ⇒ ∠BAC = 55°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• ∠BAC = (∠ABD + ∠ACE) − 180° = (110 + 125) − 180 = 55°.

NOTE

• Exterior angle of a triangle = sum of the two remote interior angles.

question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. Angle ABE = 64 degrees and angle CDE = 32 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BED?

[Figure: AB and CD are two parallel vertical segments (B, D at top; A, C at bottom). Point E lies between them, joined to B and to D, forming ∠ABE at B and ∠CDE at D.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 96.

GIVEN

• AB ∥ CD, ∠ABE = 64°, ∠CDE = 32°.

SOLUTION

• Draw a line through E parallel to both AB and CD.

• The part of ∠BED on the AB side = alternate angle with ∠ABE = 64°.

• The part on the CD side = alternate angle with ∠CDE = 32°.

• ∠BED = 64° + 32° = 96°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• When a point lies between two parallel lines (zig-zag), the middle angle = sum of the two end angles = 64 + 32 = 96°.

NOTE

• Draw an auxiliary line through the vertex parallel to the given parallels; alternate interior angles then add up.

question:
In the given figure, ABCD is a square. Angle DEC = 75 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle EFA?

[Figure: Square ABCD with A bottom-left, B bottom-right, C top-right, D top-left. Diagonal DB and line CF (F on AB) intersect at E inside the square, with ∠DEC = 75°.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 120.

GIVEN

• ABCD is a square; diagonal DB and line CF (F on AB) meet at E; ∠DEC = 75°.

SOLUTION

• ∠FEB = ∠DEC = 75° (vertically opposite, as D-E-B and C-E-F are straight lines).

• The diagonal DB bisects the corner at B, so ∠EBF = ∠DBA = 45°.

• In triangle FEB: ∠EFB = 180° − 75° − 45° = 60°.

• ∠EFA and ∠EFB are on a straight line AB, so ∠EFA = 180° − 60° = 120°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• ∠EFA = 180° − (180° − ∠DEC − 45°) = ∠DEC + 45° = 75° + 45° = 120°.

NOTE

• A diagonal of a square bisects its right angles into 45° each; use vertical angles and the straight-line (linear pair) property.
